name: KAMACITE
summary: A Dragos-designated access-development group that penetrates industrial organisations, steals and replays credentials, and enables follow-on ICS operations by teams such as ELECTRUM.
primaryFocus: Initial access, credential capture and handoff into industrial environments

stateAffiliation.assessment: KAMACITE is a Dragos behavioural cluster with overlap to Sandworm activity and an operational relationship with ELECTRUM; political attribution is inherited from those overlaps rather than asserted by Dragos for the name alone.

observedSince.label: KAMACITE activity cluster
observedSince.qualification: Dragos describes related behaviour targeting industrial organisations since at least 2014.

observedSince.label: Current expansion
observedSince.qualification: Dragos reports renewed European and U.S. activity and systematic mapping of exposed U.S. industrial devices during 2025.

designations.name: KAMACITE
designations.description: The access-development and Stage 1/early Stage 2 activity cluster profiled here.

designations.name: ELECTRUM
designations.description: A follow-on team that has received KAMACITE-enabled access and executed ICS-specific operations.

designations.name: Sandworm Team
designations.description: The broader public cluster with which Dragos reports KAMACITE activity overlaps.

designations.name: Seashell Blizzard
designations.description: A provider designation recorded by MITRE for the broader Sandworm cluster, not a direct KAMACITE alias.

assessment.text: KAMACITE specialises in gaining and maintaining access, capturing credentials and positioning follow-on teams. Dragos distinguishes this role from the teams that execute the final ICS-specific disruptive action.
The group's enduring tradecraft combines malicious attachments, credential replay, compromised third-party infrastructure, custom implants, criminal malware and native administrative tools.

In 2025, KAMACITE moved beyond generic perimeter reconnaissance to sequential scanning of HMIs, drives, meters and cellular gateways, behaviour Dragos assesses as mapping control loops across U.S. infrastructure.

technologies.name: SOHO routers and compromised third-party servers
HMIs, variable frequency drives, meters and cellular gateways

campaigns.name: Ukraine power access development
campaigns.summary: Phishing, BLACKENERGY-family malware, credential theft and network penetration established access that supported the 2015 and 2016 Ukraine electric-power operations.
campaigns.impact: KAMACITE facilitated conditions for physical disruption while Dragos attributes at least the 2016 ICS execution to ELECTRUM.

campaigns.name: U.S. energy intrusion activity
campaigns.summary: Persistent intrusion attempts against U.S. energy companies used compromised infrastructure, credential capture and replay.
campaigns.impact: Access into industrial organisations created options for later operational handoff even where no public disruptive event followed.

campaigns.name: European oil and gas conference lures
campaigns.summary: Spearphishing themed around the Gas Infrastructure Europe conference delivered commodity and custom malware against European oil and natural gas organisations.
campaigns.impact: Credential theft and endpoint access increased supply-chain and IT-to-OT pivot risk.

campaigns.name: U.S. control-loop mapping
campaigns.summary: Dragos observed four months of sequential scanning across exposed HMIs, variable frequency drives, meters and cellular gateways in U.S. infrastructure.
campaigns.impact: The sequence could reveal process relationships and operational dependencies useful for later disruption.

capabilities.name: Phish and replay captured credentials
capabilities.description: Use malicious attachments and legitimate external services to gain access, then reuse captured credentials for remote entry and movement.

capabilities.name: Develop and modify malware
capabilities.description: Deploy custom implants and adapt criminal malware while blending them with native tools and administration frameworks.

capabilities.name: Enable follow-on ICS operators
capabilities.description: Maintain access and transfer operational control to teams such as ELECTRUM for ICS-specific effects.

capabilities.name: Map exposed control-loop components
capabilities.description: Scan industrial device classes in deliberate sequence to understand process relationships.

malware.name: BLACKENERGY2 / BLACKENERGY3 / GREYENERGY
malware.description: Historical malware families associated with access, credential collection and network penetration supporting Ukraine power operations.

malware.name: Kapeka
malware.description: A backdoor used in 2024 activity against European oil and natural gas organisations.

malware.name: LummaStealer and custom Windows implants
malware.description: Rented commodity infrastructure and custom payloads used in conference-themed access campaigns.

enterprise.name: Phishing: Spearphishing Attachment
enterprise.behaviour: Malicious attachments and conference-themed lures delivered custom and commodity malware.

enterprise.name: Valid Accounts
enterprise.behaviour: Captured credentials were replayed through legitimate external services and remote access paths.

enterprise.name: OS Credential Dumping
enterprise.behaviour: Dragos assesses with moderate confidence that KAMACITE uses tools such as Mimikatz to capture credentials.

enterprise.name: Remote Services: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
enterprise.behaviour: Administrative frameworks such as PsExec supported remote execution and movement.

ics.name: Spearphishing Attachment
ics.behaviour: Targeted attachments established enterprise footholds that could be developed towards ICS networks.

ics.name: Valid Accounts
ics.behaviour: Credential replay enabled remote entry and maintained access around industrial environments.

ics.name: Remote Services
ics.behaviour: Legitimate remote access and administration paths supported movement towards control networks.

ics.name: Lateral Tool Transfer
ics.behaviour: Custom malware, criminal tools and native utilities were transferred during access development.

ics.name: Internet Accessible Device
ics.behaviour: Sequential scanning targeted exposed HMIs, drives, meters and cellular gateways during 2025.

indicatorNotice: No historical infrastructure is reproduced here. KAMACITE routinely uses compromised third-party servers, Tor relays and criminal hosting, so isolated IP matches have low durability without authentication and execution context.

defensivePriorities.name: Harden the identity path into OT
defensivePriorities.description: Require MFA for remote access, remove shared/local administrator credentials and alert on credential replay across IT and OT boundaries.

defensivePriorities.name: Detect the handoff before process access
defensivePriorities.description: Treat KAMACITE-style access as preparation for a follow-on ICS operator and escalate containment before operational credentials or diagrams are exposed.

defensivePriorities.name: Monitor sequential industrial scanning
defensivePriorities.description: Correlate probes across HMIs, drives, meters and gateways rather than triaging each exposed device independently.

defensivePriorities.name: Control unsigned execution and remote tools
defensivePriorities.description: Restrict PsExec-like administration, unsigned payloads and unexpected software execution in sensitive environments.
